absent: Common sleeping acquisition queueing, priority inheritance, timeout, and wakeup behavior beyond the thin wrappers shown.
Full layouts of mutex, read-write base, real-time base lock, and semaphore objects beyond fields visible here.
Numeric values of reader bias, writer bias, unlocked count value, contention flags, and sleep state constants.
Detailed unlock paths for read-write base and semaphore including reader release and writer release ordering.
Optimistic spinning queue behavior and full wake selection policy for queued readers and writers.

findings.text: Sleeping mutex acquisition is offered in uninterruptible, interruptible, and killable flavors, each with a default and a subclass-accepting form, plus a form accepting a separate nesting dependency object. All record caller context for dependency tracking and may block until ownership is granted.

Two acquisition helpers account the wait as input-output stall, declaring sleepability and bracketing the blocking wait with scheduler prepare and finish steps. One accepts a nesting subclass while the other uses the default subclass.

Nonblocking acquisition attempts ownership exactly once and reports success without sleeping. A nesting variant additionally records dependency acquisition on success using a caller supplied nesting object.

Mutex initialization prepares the embedded real-time base object and checks that no held lock state is being discarded. A lock dependency aware form additionally registers a wait-type dependency map from caller supplied name and class key.
Real-time waiter ordering node carries tree linkage for queue membership together with a priority value and a deadline value used to order contending waiters.

Real-time mutex waiter aggregates two ordering nodes for normal and inheritance queues, a blocked task reference, a back reference to the contended base lock, a wake condition, and an optional wound-wait acquisition context.
Real-time wake queue header extends the generic batched wake queue with one extra task reference reserved for real-time lock wakeups.

Sleeping semaphore waiter state comprises queue linkage, blocked task identity, requested access mode distinguishing read from write, an expiry instant, and a handoff marker. Companion enumerations select waiter mode, wake target policy, and owner classification for spinning decisions.

Owner word reserves its two lowest bit positions as flags for reader-owned state and for nonspinnable state. A combined mask covers exactly those flag positions, leaving higher bits for owner identity.

Semaphore count word assigns lowest position to writer-held state, next two positions to waiter-present and handoff states, highest position to read-failure state, and a reader counter field beginning at bit position eight with unit stride. Derived masks isolate writer state, reader field, combined locked state, and combined read-failure conditions.
Queued waiter expiry is based on a fraction of one timer tick around one two-hundred-fiftieth of a second, and the number of readers woken in one operation is capped at two hundred fifty six.

Reader fast path succeeds only while the reader counter remains negative and advances it by one with acquire ordering. Writer handling first holds the inner mutex, then applies a large negative shift to divert new readers into the slow path, then waits until outstanding readers drain before completing.
Priority inheritance chain traversal distinguishes a minimal walk mode from a full walk mode.

Read-write base slow paths hold the inner mutex queue lock with interrupts masked while inspecting or publishing counter state, surround the wait with contention markers, preserve and restore task sleep state across blocking, and release the inner mutex after publishing reader presence or after writer completion.

Semaphore setup clears count and owner state, initializes queue locking and an empty first-waiter anchor, and optionally initializes optimistic spinning state. Owner publication requires preemption disabled, reader ownership records the current task, and transition to nonspinnable uses an atomic update that only affects reader-owned states.

Waiter list removal requires the queue lock, refreshes the cached head when the removed entry was first, and clears waiter-present plus handoff indications when the queue becomes empty. A combined remove-and-wake helper can mark successors eligible before releasing the queue lock and then issues deferred wakeups.

Read acquisition asserts absence of inheritance blocking, attempts the fast increment, and otherwise enters a slow phase that retains the inner queue lock across the blocking call so the reader cannot be ordered behind a newly arriving writer. Success publishes one reader, releases queue locking, wakes deferred tasks, drops the inner mutex, and closes contention accounting.

Queued writer handling respects an existing handoff marker owned by the head waiter, may install handoff when locked state persists and the waiter is latency sensitive or expired, and otherwise completes acquisition when neither reader nor writer state remains while clearing handoff and possibly waiter-present. An unqueued optimistic attempt succeeds only when locked state and handoff are both absent.

Two build variants implement the same abstract read-write base operations with different blocking behavior. One forwards sleep, wake, signal sensitivity, and state save operations to sleeping semaphore style primitives, while the other forwards them to real-time lock primitives with signal sensitivity disabled and builds try operations from atomic compare exchange plus a slow try fallback.
Nonblocking mutex attempts built with real-time mutex debugging check for task context and warn plus report failure when called outside task context instead of accessing the underlying lock.

Optimistic spinning on semaphore ownership requires preemption disabled so the observed owner remains stable, re-reads owner identity and flag state to detect change, orders that check before inspecting owner execution state, and abandons spinning when rescheduling is needed, when the owner leaves the processor, or when nonspinnable state is observed.
Downgrade changes a held write position into one outstanding reader while still holding the queue lock, emitting contended-release accounting when waiters are present.
